```{r}

library(tidyverse)

chi_entertainment_clean <- readRDS("data/chi_entertainment_clean.rds")

chi_transport_clean <- readRDS("data/chi_transport_clean.rds")

source("config.R")

bnb_sample <- readRDS("data/bnb_sample.rds")

```

### Exploratory Data Analysis



```{r}

lower_48 <- state_boundaries |> 
  filter(REGION != 9 & !(STUSPS %in% c("AK", "HI")))
bnb_sample_sf |> 
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = lower_48) +
  geom_sf()
```



## Models




### Initial Model with City, Room type, and Host

```{r}
lm_bnb <- lm(log(price) ~ room_type + city + bedrooms + review_scores_rating, data = bnb_sample_sf) 
summary(lm_bnb)
```

City, Room Type, and Host already explain a large amount of variation in price. 

#### Adding an Interaction

I explore adding an interaction between the distance to coast for each city. 

```{r}
lm_bnb_2 <- lm(log(price) ~ room_type + city*log(coast_distance_km) + bedrooms + review_scores_rating, data = bnb_sample_sf) 
```

```{r}
summary(lm_bnb_2)
```

```{r}
plot(lm_bnb_2)
```

Chicago and DC have `coast_distance_km` that are too high. Including an interaction does not make sense here because the values of `coast_distance_km` do not overlap. Cities without coastal offerings will be removed from the analysis. See the following plots and EDA.

#### Cities included in the final model

```{r}
bnb_sample_sf_coast <- bnb_sample_sf |> 
   filter(city %in% c("Boston", "LA", "SF", "NYC"))
```

```{r}
bnb_sample_sf |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = coast_distance_km, y = log(price), color = city)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_color_viridis_d() +
  geom_smooth(formula = y ~ x, method = "lm")
```
DC and Boston have `coast_distance_km` values that are different from the other cities. 

```{r}
bnb_sample_sf_coast |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = coast_distance_km, y = log(price), color = city)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_color_viridis_d() +
  geom_smooth(formula = y ~ x, method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "Distance to Coast (in km)",
    title = "Scatterplot of log(price) vs Distance to Coast by City",
    subtitle = "(for 8739 Listings)"
  ) +
  theme_gray()
```

```{r}
bnb_sample_sf_coast |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = coast_distance_km)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(fill = city), bins = 40) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  labs(
    title = "Histogram of Distance to Coast by City",
    x = "Distance to Coast (in km)",
    y = "Frequency",
    subtitle = "(for 8739 Listings)"
  ) + 
  theme_bw()
```

### OSM Data

```{r}
chi_bnb <- bnb_sample_sf |> 
  filter(city == "Chicago")
chi_bbox <-st_bbox(chi_bnb) |> 
  st_as_sfc()
chi_bbox_buffered <- chi_bbox |> 
  st_transform(26916) |>  #code for projection to meters in Chicago 
  st_buffer(dist = 5000) |> 
  st_transform(4326)


```

```{r}
ggplot() +
  annotation_map_tile() + 
  geom_sf(data = chi_bbox_buffered, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = chi_bbox, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = chi_bnb)
```

### KDE for `chi_entertainment_clean`


```{r}
window <- chi_bbox_buffered |> 
  st_transform(crs = 26916) |> 
  as.owin()
```
```{r}
coords <- chi_entertainment_clean |> 
  st_filter(st_transform(chi_bbox_buffered, 26916)) |> 
  st_coordinates()

pp_entertainment <- ppp(
  x = coords[,1],
  y = coords[,2],
  window = window
)
```
```{r}
plot(pp_entertainment)
```

### KDE for `chi_kde_transport_table`
```{r}
window <- chi_bbox_buffered |> 
  st_transform(crs = 26916) |> 
  as.owin()
```
```{r}
coords <- chi_entertainment_clean |> 
  st_filter(st_transform(chi_bbox_buffered, 26916)) |> 
  st_coordinates()

pp_entertainment <- ppp(
  x = coords[,1],
  y = coords[,2],
  window = window
)
```
```{r}
plot(pp_entertainment)
```
**Note:** Added the `st_filter()` command because some points were outside the ppp. This needs to be investigated, but it is likely because of st_transform or osm data bringing polygons that are beyond the border. 

```{r}
bw.ppl(pp_entertainment)
```

Likelihood Cross-Validation (`spatstat::bw.ppl()`) identified an optimal bandwidth scale near 926m. For model simplicity and interpretability, $\sigma = 1,000\text{m}  (1 \text{km})$ was selected, representing a standard 10-to-12 minute walk for pedestrians."

A fixed bandwidth of 1,000 m was used to estimate entertainment activity density. This scale was chosen to capture neighborhood-level patterns rather than highly localized concentrations of individual establishments.

```{r}
sigma = 1000 #1000 meters based on the existing crs = 26916
kde_entertainment <- density.ppp(
  pp_entertainment,
  sigma = sigma
)
```

```{r}
plot(kde_entertainment)
```


```{r}
chi_entertainment_raster <- kde_entertainment |> 
  rast() 
  ggplot(data = chi_entertainment_raster) +
    geom_sf(data = chi_entertainment_clean, alpha = 1) +
  geom_spatraster(data = chi_entertainment_raster, alpha = 0.5) + 
 
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma") +
  annotation_map_tile(alpha = 0.3)+
    
  coord_sf(crs = 26916) 

```
```{r}
chi_mean_val <- global(chi_entertainment_raster, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)$mean
chi_sd_val <- global(chi_entertainment_raster, "sd", na.rm = TRUE)$sd

chi_entertainment_raster_z <- (chi_entertainment_raster - chi_mean_val)/chi_sd_val

```



```{r}
#Display KDE
kde_plot <- chi_entertainment_raster
kde_plot[kde_plot < 1e-6] <- NA  # Make zero-density transparent

ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = kde_plot*100000, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    begin = 0.2,
    option = "magma", 
    na.value = "transparent",
    name = "Venue Density\n(Index x 10^5)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Chicago Entertainment Venue Density",
    subtitle = "Kernel Density Estimation (σ = 1000m) used in Pricing Model",
    x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  annotation_map_tile(alpha = 0.3)+
  coord_sf(crs = 26916)+
  theme_minimal()

```

### Standardizing KDE

```{r}
chi_entertainment_raster_z |> 
  as.data.frame(xy = TRUE) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = lyr.1)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, color = "black", fill = "lightblue")
```

### Log-transforming KDE and then standardizing due to the skew

```{r}
chi_entertainment_raster_log <- log(chi_entertainment_raster+ 1e-6)


chi_mean_val_log <- global(chi_entertainment_raster_log, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)$mean
chi_sd_val_log <- global(chi_entertainment_raster_log, "sd", na.rm = TRUE)$sd

chi_entertainment_raster_z_log <- (chi_entertainment_raster_log - chi_mean_val_log)/chi_sd_val_log
```
```{r}
chi_entertainment_raster_z_log |> 
  as.data.frame(xy = TRUE) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = lyr.1)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, color = "black", fill = "lightblue")
```



```{r}
#Display standardized KDE
kde_plot_z_log <- chi_entertainment_raster_z_log %>%
  ifel(test = . < 0, NA, no = .)
#kde_plot[kde_plot < 1e-6] <- NA  # Make zero-density transparent

ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = kde_plot_z_log, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    begin = 0.2,
    option = "magma", 
    na.value = "transparent",
    name = "Relative Venue Density"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Chicago Entertainment Venue Density",
    subtitle = "Log-transformed Standardized Kernel Density Estimation (σ = 1000m)",
    x = "Longitude", 
    y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  annotation_map_tile(alpha = 0.4)+
  coord_sf(crs = 26916)+
  theme_minimal()

```


### Comparing Models with KDE, Neighborhood

```{r}
chi_bnb_data <- bnb_sample_sf |> 
  filter(city == "Chicago") |> 
  st_transform(26916) 
```
```{r}
chi_model <- lm(log(price) ~ room_type + bedrooms + review_scores_rating + has_pool, data = chi_bnb_data) 
```
```{r}
summary(chi_model)
```

```{r}
extracted_values<- extract(chi_entertainment_raster, chi_bnb_data)
chi_bnb_data$kde_value <- extracted_values[,2]

extracted_values_log <- extract(chi_entertainment_raster_z_log, chi_bnb_data)
chi_bnb_data$kde_value_log_z <- extracted_values_log[,2]
```


```{r}
chi_model_2 <- lm(log(price) ~ room_type + accommodates + bathrooms + bedrooms+ review_scores_rating + has_pool + kde_value, data = chi_bnb_data) 
```




```{r}
chi_model_2 |> summary()
plot(chi_model_2, which = 1, add.smooth = F, id.n = 0 )
plot(chi_model_2, which = 2, id.n = 0)
```
```{r}
chi_model_2 |> 
 vif()
```

The variable `has_pool` is no longer significant when using `kde_value`. This could be because Airbnbs with pools were already in neighborhoods closer to downtown, and the KDE can explain this variation. 

```{r}
chi_bnb_data |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = has_pool, y = kde_value)) +
  geom_boxplot() + 
  labs(
    title = "Kernel Density Estimate (KDE) by Pool Amenity",
    subtitle = "(for 511 Airbnb observations in Chicago)",
    x = "Has Pool?",
    y = "KDE Value"
  ) +
  theme_bw() 
```

```{r}
chi_model_3 <- lm(log(price) ~ room_type + accommodates + bathrooms + bedrooms+ review_scores_rating + has_pool + kde_value_log_z, data = chi_bnb_data) 
```
```{r}
summary(chi_model_3)
plot(chi_model_3, which = 1, add.smooth = F, id.n = 0 )
plot(chi_model_3, which = 2, id.n = 0)
chi_model_3 |> 
  vif()
```
All adjusted GVIF values are reasonable, and less than the equivalent VIF = 5 threshold. There is some multicollinarity, but it is not severe.


```{r}
chi_model_4 <- lm(log(price) ~ room_type + accommodates + bathrooms + bedrooms+ review_scores_rating+ has_pool + kde_value + neighbourhood, data = chi_bnb_data) 
```
```{r}
summary(chi_model_4)
```

While introducing the indicator variable `neighbourhood` increased the multiple $R^2$ from 0.608 to 0.677, the Adjusted $R^2$ did not change by much (0.601 to 0.613) while adding all of the neighborhoods. Moreover, multiple sparse neighborhoods yielded observations with leverage = 1, signaling overfitting, and nearly 20% of the observations have been deleted due to missing data. Lastly, the `neighbourhood` predictor is specific to Chicago, whereas `kde_value` can be computed for any city. Therefore, the KDE model will be used.
